Calculate the average number of living kin over time

Source: R/extract_kin.R
count_kin.Rd

Count, for each person living at each requested time, the living relatives recorded within generations parent steps on each side, by relationship, and average them over living persons.

Usage

count_kin(population, times, generations = 2, by = NULL, relationships = NULL)

Arguments

population

A hammel_population with a known end_time no earlier than the requested times.

times

A numeric vector of finite time points in years.

generations

Nonnegative whole number of parent generations on each side, default 2, which covers parents, children, grandparents, grandchildren, siblings, aunts and uncles, nieces and nephews, and first cousins.

by

NULL (default) or a character vector of the ego's characteristics at each time to count separately: "sex" and declared group dimensions, such as "race".

relationships

NULL (default) for all relationships, or a nonempty character vector of unique relationship names within generations, such as "first_cousin". Retains the usual row order and ego denominators.

Value

A tibble with time, the by columns, relationship, persons (living egos), kin (their living kin of that type), mean_kin (kin / persons) and share_with_kin (share of egos with at least one). mean_kin and share_with_kin are NA with no egos. Every time, stratum and selected relationship within generations has a row. Rows vary by time fastest, then the by variables in order, then relationship.

Details

Counts use recorded parent links only. A starting population without recorded parents has no recorded kin, so counts are too low until two or three generations have been simulated. Allow a burn-in before interpreting them. Relatives share kin, so egos are not independent.

The following named relationships are available:

  • "parent"

  • "child"

  • "grandparent"

  • "grandchild"

  • "sibling"

  • "aunt_uncle"

  • "niece_nephew"

  • "first_cousin"

  • "great_grandparent" (requires generations = 3)

  • "great_grandchild" (requires generations = 3)

  • "great_aunt_uncle" (requires generations = 3)

  • "great_niece_nephew" (requires generations = 3)

  • "first_cousin_once_removed" (requires generations = 3)

  • "second_cousin" (requires generations = 3)

See also

extract_kin()

Examples

population <- generate_uniform_population(1000)
model <- hammel_model() |>
  set_population(population) |>
  set_mortality(usa_2000_mortality) |>
  set_fertility(usa_2000_fertility) |>
  set_union_formation(
    "on_demand",
    matching = age_gap_matching_model(3, 5)
  )
result <- run_simulation(model, years = 100, seed = 42)
count_kin(result, 100, relationships = "first_cousin")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>    time relationship persons   kin mean_kin share_with_kin
#>   <dbl> <chr>          <int> <int>    <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1   100 first_cousin    1263  7282     5.77          0.839
